owner: Repository maintainer (human approver of the Phase 14 exception; role-based, no personal data)
rationale: A patched release of `braces` does not exist: 3.0.3 is the latest npm release (published 2024-05-21) and the advisory lists no first patched version, so there is nothing to remediate to today. Request-time reachability is not demonstrated: the package is reached only through the Tailwind CSS build CLI and the ESLint tooling (zero application imports, static build-time glob literals only). Exposure is therefore limited to build and development tooling, not served requests. The exception is temporary and expires automatically; it does not declare the package safe, and any additional advisory, package, severity change, CVSS change, version change, or expiry rejects the audit and fails the gate. Upstream status: fix PR micromatch/braces#72 is open and unmerged on a third-party fork with no maintainer engagement, and the upstream repository has had no push since 2025-01-19.
reviewInstructions: Re-review at least every 7 days from the approval date, and immediately on any `braces` registry publish. Patch-check command: `npm view braces dist-tags.latest` — if the output is anything other than `3.0.3`, a patched release exists; remove this exception, bump `braces`, and re-run the audit gates. Also check the upstream fix state: `gh pr view 72 --repo micromatch/braces --json state,merged`. At the expiry date the policy exits 1 unconditionally, CI goes red, and this exception must be removed and either remediated or re-authorized with fresh evidence. Do not extend the expiry by editing this file without a new risk-acceptance decision. Companion follow-up: moving `tailwindcss-animate` from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` would permanently remove the production-closure exposure (it is the sole production-classified dependent of `tailwindcss`), but the bare audit's ESLint chain would still require an exception.
